Council  2026-08-17 14:05
  A UK company sells SaaS to EU consumers and US businesses. What are the VAT and US
  sales-tax obligations, and where do they interact?

  panel: ~openai/gpt-latest ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest ~google/gemini-pro-latest
  ~x-ai/grok-latest
  judge: ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest · synthesis: ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest →
  anthropic/claude-opus-5

ANSWER
──────
  Two separate regimes apply and they do not overlap.

  For EU consumers the UK company must register for VAT under the non-Union OSS scheme
  and charge the customer's local rate from the first sale — there is no threshold. For
  US business customers, SaaS taxability varies by state and the reverse-charge concept
  does not exist.

DISAGREED  (1)
──────────────
  the panel split here — treat these as open questions, not settled answers
  Whether B2B sales to EU businesses need OSS registration
    ~openai/gpt-latest
      No — B2B supplies are covered by the reverse charge, so OSS is not needed for
      them.
    ~google/gemini-pro-latest
      Partially — the reverse charge applies only where the customer's VAT number is
      validated; unvalidated customers must be treated as B2C.

AGREED  (2)
───────────
  • Non-Union OSS registration is required for EU B2C sales from the first euro; there
    is no de minimis threshold.
  • US sales tax is determined state by state, and economic nexus thresholds are
    evaluated per state.

RAISED BY ONE MODEL  (1)
────────────────────────
  ~x-ai/grok-latest
      Several US states tax SaaS as tangible personal property rather than a service,
      which changes the sourcing rule.

RAISED BY SOME  (1)
───────────────────
  ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest, ~google/gemini-pro-latest
      Invoicing must show the customer's VAT number for the reverse charge to be
      defensible on audit.

NOT COVERED BY ANYONE  (1)
──────────────────────────
  • No model addressed the UK's own VAT position on the same supplies after the Brexit
    transition.
